issues.original: AI features in Google Search use techniques such as retrieval-augmented generation and query fan-out to pull from pages Google already understands.
issues.replacement: AI features in Google Search can use techniques such as query fan-out to pull from pages Google already understands.
issues.reason: The supplied Google source discusses query fan-out but does not establish retrieval-augmented generation; keeping the stronger technical claim would make an unsupported statement about how Google's AI features work.

assessment.intent: Give busy Okanagan business owners an answer-first, practical way to qualify for Google Search and AI features without pretending there is a separate AI-only checklist.
assessment.specificity: Strong. It stays grounded in Google and OpenAI's stated requirements, avoids invented case studies, uses at most one implicit project reference, and gives concrete page, navigation, local and measurement actions.
assessment.evidence: Good overall. The one unsupported technical claim about retrieval-augmented generation needs removal; the rest avoids fake percentages, proven claims, universal guarantees and invented client outcomes.
assessment.voice: Close to Michael's preferred register: clear, Canadian, practical, owner-centred, sceptical of hype and respectful of the reader's time. It keeps useful opinions without self-praise.
assessment.usefulAsset: Yes. The article's structure, title, factual boundaries, local focus and measured AI-search guidance are worth keeping with only a narrow factual repair.
